ideas: Housing is far less affordable than before
Competition for good jobs is much tougher
More opportunities and technology than parents had

phrases.phrase: get a foot in the door
phrases.meaning: get a first chance in a career
confidence you won't lose your job
extremely hard to win or succeed

model: Yes, I think young people have it harder than their parents did, at least in some important ways. First, housing is far less affordable. When my parents got married in the nineties, they bought a small house in Hanoi after saving for about five years. Today, with sky-high property prices, most of my friends are told they'd need twenty years or more to buy a flat. Another reason is that the job market is fiercely competitive. Although more young people have university degrees, getting a foot in the door is really difficult, and many graduates are hired on short contracts with little job security. My father had a job for life in a state company, whereas I've already changed companies three times, and I often feel under constant pressure to learn new skills. Of course, we do have a wider range of opportunities, like travelling and working online, and in many ways we're better off. But in terms of security and housing, I believe our generation definitely has it harder.
